summary: A dizzying blend of ancient temples and neon-lit skyscrapers, Tokyo delivers world-class food, unmatched transit, and endless neighbourhoods to explore.

restaurants.name: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten
restaurants.description: Legendary 10-seat sushi counter that earned the world's attention. Reserve months ahead.

restaurants.name: Ichiran Ramen
restaurants.description: Solo ramen booths let you customise your tonkotsu broth in peace. Open 24 hours.

restaurants.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
restaurants.description: Fresh seafood stalls and tamagoyaki shops surrounding the old fish market.

restaurants.name: Narisawa
restaurants.description: Innovative 'Satoyama cuisine' drawing from Japan's forests and farmlands.

restaurants.name: Kura Sushi
restaurants.description: Conveyor-belt sushi chain with plates starting at ¥115. Perfect for families.

restaurants.name: Kyubey Ginza
restaurants.description: Established 1936, this Ginza institution serves exquisite Edo-mae sushi.

restaurants.name: Afuri Ramen
restaurants.description: Yuzu shio ramen with a delicate citrusy broth. Multiple locations citywide.

restaurants.name: Tempura Kondo
restaurants.description: Tempura elevated to art form — seasonal vegetables and seafood in a Ginza high-rise.

restaurants.name: Ippudo Ramen
restaurants.description: Global chain born in Fukuoka. Rich Hakata-style tonkotsu done right.

restaurants.name: Monja Street, Tsukishima
restaurants.description: A whole street dedicated to monjayaki — Tokyo's gooey savoury pancake.

restaurants.name: Tapas Molecular Bar
restaurants.description: 30-course molecular gastronomy counter at the Mandarin Oriental.

restaurants.name: Hamacho Genki Shokudo
restaurants.description: Classic teishoku lunch sets beloved by Tokyo salarymen. Cash only.

activities.name: Senso-ji Temple at Dawn
activities.description: Arrive before 6 AM to have Asakusa's iconic temple almost to yourself.

activities.name: teamLab Planets
activities.description: Immersive digital art museum in Toyosu — wade through water mirrors and floating flowers.

activities.name: Shibuya Crossing & Scramble Observation
activities.description: Watch the world's busiest pedestrian crossing from the Mag's Park observation deck.

activities.name: Tokyo DisneySea
activities.description: Often ranked the world's best theme park — themed ports and spectacular shows.

activities.name: Shinjuku Golden Gai Bar-hop
activities.description: Navigate 200+ tiny bars crammed into six alleyways — each fits a dozen people.

activities.name: Tsukiji Fish Market Tour
activities.description: Early-morning guided tuna auction viewing followed by a sushi breakfast.

activities.name: Mount Fuji Day Trip
activities.description: Take the Shinkansen to Kawaguchiko for iconic lake-with-Fuji views. Season dependent.

activities.name: Akihabara Electronics & Anime
activities.description: Tokyo's otaku epicentre — multi-floor arcades, figurine shops, and maid cafés.

activities.name: Yanaka Cemetery Walk
activities.description: Stroll through one of Tokyo's last old-shitamachi neighbourhoods — temples, cats, and craft shops.

activities.name: Sumo Practice Tour
activities.description: Watch morning keiko (training) at a sumo stable in Ryogoku. Advance booking essential.

activities.name: Tokyo Tower Observatory
activities.description: Classic city panorama including Fuji on clear winter days.

activities.name: Harajuku Takeshita Street
activities.description: Japan's wildest fashion street — crepe stands, vintage shops, and Harajuku style.

spots.name: Shibuya Crossing from Shibuya Sky
spots.description: Rooftop observation deck above the scramble — magical at blue hour.

spots.name: Senso-ji Nakamise Approach
spots.description: Storm gate and paper lanterns glow red at dawn.

spots.name: Shinjuku Kabukicho Neons
spots.description: Densest concentration of neon signs in the world — walk Golden Gai alley.

spots.name: Yanaka Old Town Rooftops
spots.description: Traditional tile rooflines and old Showa signage.

spots.name: Ueno Park Cherry Blossoms
spots.description: April sakura tunnels with rows of lanterns. Season: late March–early April.

spots.name: teamLab Planets Water Mirror
spots.description: Mirror-floor room with floating digital flowers — long exposure essential.

spots.name: Tokyo Station Marunouchi Facade
spots.description: Red-brick Taisho-era station beautifully lit at night.

spots.name: Meguro River Canal
spots.description: Cherry blossoms arch over the canal in spring; lanterns in summer.

spots.name: Hamarikyu Gardens Teahouse
spots.description: Traditional garden with skyscrapers as backdrop — surreal contrast.

spots.name: Shinjuku from Takashimaya Rooftop
spots.description: Free rooftop with sweeping NS Building and skyscraper views.

photography.goldenHourNotes: Tokyo's golden hour lasts 30–40 minutes. In winter the setting sun often aligns perfectly with Mount Fuji from Chuo Line trains. Typhoon season (Sep–Oct) brings dramatic storm light.

weather.seasonality: Spring (Mar–May) brings cherry blossoms; autumn (Oct–Nov) shows stunning foliage. Avoid the rainy season (Jun–Jul) and typhoon risk (Sep–Oct). Winters are dry and crisp with occasional Fuji views.
weather.summary: Four distinct seasons. Spring and autumn are ideal. Summers are hot and humid with a typhoon season risk.

hotels.name: Aman Tokyo
hotels.description: Dramatic 33rd-floor lobby inspired by traditional Japanese paper screens. Best city views.

hotels.name: Trunk Hotel
hotels.description: Design-forward hotel with a strong social ethos — rooftop fire pit and local craft beers.

hotels.name: Khaosan Tokyo Origami
hotels.description: Well-run hostel in historic Asakusa — private rooms and dorms, steps from Senso-ji.
